transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I appreciate us coming together to review the incident resolution plan before it goes to the district director for certification. As the school testing coordinator, I want to make sure we're aligning our plan with state protocol, so I have some important information to share about the scope of the impact. Before I do, I'd like to hear from others on the call — particularly regarding the draft plan's proposal to cancel the entire session and retest all students. Has anyone reviewed whether that approach matches what the state incident protocol actually requires?

transcript.text: Thank you, Ms. Shah. I appreciate you opening the floor. Before we discuss whether canceling the entire session and retesting all students online aligns with state protocol, I need to flag something important. I reviewed the affected students' files this morning, and there's an accommodation issue we need to address — one of the six affected students has an approved accommodation requiring a paper-based test, not an online retest. I'll go ahead and formally attach that accommodation documentation to the incident record, but we'll need to adjust the draft plan to account for a paper testing option for that student.

Yesterday, I completed a reconciliation using the completed seating chart and proctor statement, which identify exactly six students who could see the answer-review screen. The state incident protocol requires invalidating only those six students' scores and offering their retest within 10 school days — not canceling the entire session. This means the draft plan's proposal to cancel the entire session and retest all students goes beyond what state protocol requires. However, I should note that this reconciliation result has not yet been entered in the district incident tracker, so we'll need to make sure that gets updated as part of our revisions.
